title: Insulin preparations: bolus insulins built to release monomers fast, basal insulins built to release them slowly, and premixed pens that combine both

groups.title: Bolus — covers a meal
groups.desc: Built to release monomers from the hexamer fast. Give around the meal; the dose can be skipped if the meal is skipped.

sections.subhead: Rapid-acting analogues · 0–15 min before a meal

drugs.name: Insulin lispro
drugs.moa: Order of proline and lysine in the B chain reversed → fewer hexamers.

drugs.name: Insulin glulisine
drugs.moa: Asparagine → lysine, lysine → glutamic acid; zinc-free formulation.

drugs.name: Fast-acting insulin aspart
drugs.moa: Standard aspart plus nicotinamide and arginine → faster absorption. Closest match to the post-meal surge.

drugs.name: Regular human insulin
drugs.moa: Unmodified human insulin, so it must dissociate from hexamers before it is absorbed.

lines.label: Only:
lines.text: the ONLY insulin that can be given intravenously → diabetic ketoacidosis, hyperkalemia.

after.label: Remember:
after.text: analogues are NOT more effective at lowering HbA1c than human insulin — they are safer and more convenient (less early-night hypoglycemia, fewer bedtime snacks).

groups.title: Basal — covers the fasting state
groups.desc: Hexamer stabilized (protamine, zinc, self-aggregation, albumin binding) so monomers release slowly. Flat or minimal peak.

drugs.name: NPH (neutral protamine Hagedorn)
drugs.moa: Human insulin complexed with protamine and zinc.

lines.label: Watch:
lines.text: more nocturnal hypoglycemia than the basal analogues.

drugs.name: Insulin glargine
drugs.moa: Two extra arginines, asparagine → glycine → forms microprecipitates at neutral pH under the skin.

lines.label: Note:
lines.text: less nocturnal hypoglycemia than human insulin.

drugs.name: Insulin detemir
drugs.moa: Myristoylated (fatty acid added) → self-aggregation into dihexamers plus albumin binding.

drugs.name: Insulin degludec
drugs.moa: Multi-hexamers form after injection, plus albumin binding.

drugs.name: Insulin icodec
drugs.moa: Fatty diacid → albumin-bound depot, with lower receptor affinity → flat, ultra-long profile.

after.label: Rules:
after.text: basal insulins are never used in pumps, and most must not be mixed with another insulin before injection.

groups.title: Biphasic — premixed
groups.desc: A protamine-bound basal component and a free bolus analogue in one pen.

lines.label: Against:
lines.text: less flexibility — the least physiological regimen.
